subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What public capability taxonomy, grant storage model, default-deny upgrade behavior, enforcement boundary, and audit owner should OpenClaw adopt for skills/tools?
rationale: The issue defines security semantics, public plugin/skill metadata, persisted grant or policy state, and compatibility behavior that automation cannot infer from existing name-based policies or hook-time approvals.

options.title: Approve phased core capability model
options.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics and design grants, execution-boundary checks, audit storage, and rollout semantics behind a maintainer-approved contract before default-deny enforcement ships.

options.title: Limit to advisory descriptors first
options.body: Add visible capability declarations and inspection/status output while keeping enforcement in existing tool-policy, approval, and hook surfaces until a later RFC resolves grants.

options.title: Keep governance plugin-only
options.body: Narrow or close the core item if maintainers decide current hooks plus external governance plugins are the intended boundary for this policy class.

recommendation.title: Approve phased core capability model
recommendation.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics and design grants, execution-boundary checks, audit storage, and rollout semantics behind a maintainer-approved contract before default-deny enforcement ships.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security posture, gateway enforcement, plugin/skill API design, and product rollout; steipete is the strongest visible owner from discussion and adjacent history.
